title: Remark A
body_md: The assumption $f(z)f'(z)/z \neq 0$, $z \in \mathbb U$, in Definition A is redundant. In 1979, Sakaguchi and Fukui \emph{\cite{Sakaguchi-Fukui-1979}} established that $\Re\{J_{\alpha}[f](z)\}> 0$ for $z \in \mathbb U$, implies $f(z)f'(z)/z \neq 0$, $z \in \mathbb U$.
head: environment

label: Theorem A
title: Theorem A
body_md: \label{Theorem A}\emph{\cite{Miller-Mocanu-Reade-1973}} If $f\in\mathcal{M}_{\alpha}(\mathbb{U})$, then it is starlike and univalent in $\mathbb{U}$. Moreover, if $\alpha\geq 1$, then $f$ is convex for $|z|<1$ and if $\alpha\leq -1$, then $1/f(1/z)$ is convex for $|z| > 1$.

title: Theorem C
body_md: \emph{\cite{Miller-1973}} Let $f\in \mathcal{M}_\alpha(\mathbb{U})$ for $\alpha>0$ and be given by $f(z)=z+\sum_{n=2}^{\infty}a_n(\alpha)z^n$. Then $|a_2(\alpha)|\leq 2/(1+\alpha)$. The inequality is sharp.

title: Remark B
body_md:
For $\alpha = 0$, inequality \eqref{TheoE1} reduces to the class $\mathcal{S}^*_{\beta}(\mathbb{U})$ of starlike functions of order $\beta$, yielding $H_2(2) \le (1 - \beta)^2$, as established in \emph{\cite{Lee-2013}} \emph{(\text{see also} \cite{Cho-2018,Krishna-Ramreddy-2012})}.

\noindent For $\beta = 0$ the bounds in \eqref{TheoE2} reduce to \eqref{TheoD1} in Theorem D.
	
\noindent When $\alpha = 1$, \eqref{TheoE2} gives
\begin{align*}
H_2(2) \le (1 - \beta)^2 \frac{36 - 36\beta + 17\beta^2}{144(2 - 2\beta + \beta^2)},
\end{align*}
which represents a non-sharp bound for the class $\mathcal{K}_{\beta}(\mathbb{U})$ of convex functions of order $\beta$ obtained in \emph{\cite{Krishna-Ramreddy-2012}}. This bound yields the sharp value $1/8$ for $\alpha = 1$ and $\beta = 0$.

label: Th-1
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{Th-1}Let $\mathbb{B}$ be the unit ball in a complex Banach space ${\mathbb X}$. Let $f\in\mathcal{H}(\mathbb{B},\mathbb{C})$ with $f(0)=1$ and $F(z)=zf(z)\in\mathcal{M}_{\alpha}(\mathbb{B})$. Then $F\in\mathcal{S}^*(\mathbb{B})$. If $\alpha\geq 1$, then $F\in\mathcal{K}_B(\mathbb{B})$. Moreover if $F(z)=zf(z)\in\mathcal{M}_{\beta}(\mathbb{B})$, then $F(z)=zf(z)\in\mathcal{M}_{\alpha}(\mathbb{B})$ for all $\alpha,
 \beta\in\mathbb{R}$, $0\leq \alpha/\beta\leq 1$.

label: pro-1
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{pro-1} Let $f \in \mathcal{S}(\mathbb{U})$, $u \in {\mathbb X}$ with $\|u\| = 1$ and $l_{u} \in T(u)$. Then $F$ defined by
$F(z)=\frac{f(l_{u}(z))}{l_{u}(z)}z$ belongs to $\mathcal{M}_{\alpha}(\mathbb{B})$ if and only if $f \in \mathcal{M}_{\alpha}(\mathbb{U})$.

label: pro-2
title: Proposition
body_md: \label{pro-2} Let $f \in \mathcal{H}(\mathbb{B},\mathbb{C})$ with $f(0)=1$ and $F(z)=f(z)z$. Let $g(\zeta)=f(\zeta z_0)\zeta$, where $\zeta\in\mathbb{U}$ and $z_0\in\partial \mathbb{B}$ is fixed. Then $g\in\mathcal{M}_{\alpha}(\mathbb{U})$ if and only if $F\in\mathcal{M}_{\alpha}(\mathbb{B})$.
